findings.issue: wl3p asserts only the probe's preconditions (same size, v = 2 bytes, mtime put back). It does not assert that a stale bytecode file was ever there to be trusted. wl3/wl4 only go red when the round-0 gate's interpreter actually writes bytecode. Nothing in tools/sweep-selftests.py or tests/_harness.py scrubs PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE (grep found no hit), so a developer or runner that exports it makes the hazard absent. Then wl3/wl4 would pass with the generator switch deleted, and wl3p would not notice.
findings.resolution: Add to wl3p (or a sibling case) a direct assertion that no mine bytecode exists after round 0, under src/__pycache__ and under PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX if set. That goes red on a regression of the generator switch whatever the timing or ambient env, and the mtime probe stays as the end-to-end check.
